answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor cryptographic attestation chains to a hardware root of trust, then submit zero-knowledge proofs validating distinct execution histories. Staking contracts query this identity atlas and enforce an exponential staking bond curve: each duplicate peer in a cluster requires exponentially higher capital exhaustion. An adaptive willow tree topology isolates unproven nodes, while honeypot tasks mirror verified workloads to trap swarms with superlinear penalties.
